stem: Which of the following is correct regarding mycobacteria?

options.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis PCR can be performed on any isolate taken from a patient with suspected tuberculosis
Anti-microbial susceptibility testing cannot be performed on mycobacterial species
If an organism grows in the laboratory within 2-3 days, it cannot be a mycobacterial species because these types of organisms are slow-growing
Only Mycobacterium tuberculosis is pathogenic in humans

explanation: Most mycobacteria are slow-growing, but some species are rapid growers and may produce visible growth within 2–3 days. The other statements are incorrect: PCR is not performed on any isolate indiscriminately, susceptibility testing can be done for mycobacteria, and several non-tuberculous mycobacterial species are pathogenic in humans.
rationale: The only accurate statement is that some mycobacteria can grow rapidly in culture; therefore, growth within 2–3 days does not exclude the genus.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. PCR for M. tuberculosis is not done on any isolate from suspected TB; it depends on the specimen and laboratory method.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing is performed for mycobacterial species when indicated.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Rapid-growing mycobacteria can grow within a few days, so early growth does not exclude mycobacteria.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. Non-tuberculous mycobacteria can also cause human disease.
